job.style: a passage that starts from a common wrong idea and corrects it

response.passage: Many students believe that light only bends when it enters a liquid like water, but refraction is actually a universal phenomenon occurring whenever light travels between any two transparent media of different optical densities. This bending happens precisely at the boundary separating the two media, not after the light has traveled deep inside. When we discuss lenses, it is a common error to confuse them with mirrors. While a mirror uses reflection, a lens relies on refraction. Consequently, the mathematical relationship for lenses is 1/v - 1/u = 1/f, which is distinct from the mirror formula. Furthermore, the power of a lens is defined as the reciprocal of its focal length in meters. This means that a lens with a higher power actually possesses a shorter focal length, as the light is bent more sharply. Finally, remember that virtual images are not 'invisible' just because they are not real; they are perfectly visible to our eyes even though they cannot be captured on a screen. Similarly, light rays do not simply stop at the image position; they continue to travel through the optical system, forming the image through their convergence or apparent divergence. Understanding these distinctions is crucial for mastering the behavior of light in various optical devices.
response.summary: Refraction occurs at the boundary of any two transparent media and follows different mathematical rules than reflection. Lens power is inversely related to focal length, and virtual images remain visible despite not being real.
